summary.intent: Get the 16 open PRs in the caliper repo into a mergeable state by dispatching worker agents to resolve merge conflicts with `main` and address review findings.
summary.outcome: Workers are running on all eight conflicting PRs (#323, #327, #335, #345, #348, #349, #353, #362), but none has delivered a final report yet. Earlier, #324 had its conflict resolved and #359 needed no code change; the #362 worker has so far sent only interim notices while waiting on CI.

repo: Eight of the 16 open PRs conflicted with `main`, and several clean PRs were 60-88 commits behind it, so their CI results reflect old code.
A PR can pass CI alone and then fail once combined with newer tests. #349 did exactly this.
Tests that build a temp project without `typescript` and assert exact diagnostics fail on CI after merging with `main`. The NAPI test failed the same way before.
To mimic CI, Rust tests should run from a copy of the repo with no ancestor `node_modules`.
#291 is the release bot's PR and manages its own sync. #367 is dependabot's and was 0 behind with CI still queued.
Layer-collapse logic in #324: a union like `Omit<Big,'p0'> | Big` keeps `p0` in the layer, and a layer counts as 'collapsed' only if it lists members.
Review-finding dismissals can be denied by the permission classifier. The earlier 13 were denied, though later ones succeeded.

code.finding: Evidence used to dismiss the 'not re-measured' review finding on #324.

workflow: Subagent task notifications can be interim ('waiting on its own background work'). Wait for the final SubagentHandback report instead of treating them as results.
Giving each conflicting PR to a separate worktree-based worker lets conflict resolution run in parallel.
Leave clean-but-stale PRs untouched until the user decides whether to merge `main` into them, since that pushes to their branches.

friction: The permission classifier denied the first batch of 13 review-finding dismissals.
The #362 worker sent repeated interim notices while blocked on CI, so there was nothing actionable to report.
#348, #349 and #353 had no worker until late, so they trail the other conflicting PRs.
The CI result for #367 is still queued, with no jobs started.
open_items: Wait for final reports from the workers on #323, #327, #335, #345, #348, #349, #353 and #362.
Decide whether to merge `main` into the clean-but-stale PRs (#343, #346, #347, #352, #359, #324) so CI re-verifies the combined state.
Retry the 13 previously denied review-finding dismissals if the user still wants them.
Check #324 CI and confirm its remaining finding clears when the review re-runs.
